hints: Look at the start and finish levels on the diagram, the left side is reactants and the right side is products for the forward reaction.
Notice the products finish 20 kJ mol-1 higher than the reactants, so work out what that means for forward and backward ΔH.
Remember activation energy is measured from the starting reactants up to the very top of the hump, so add the two gaps together.
walkthrough:
**Find the enthalpy change for the forward reaction**

Think of enthalpy change as products minus reactants. Here products are higher than reactants.

$$\Delta H_{forward} = +20 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

**Decide if forward is exo or endo, and reverse the sign for backward**

Going uphill in energy means heat is taken in, so forward is endothermic. The backward reaction goes downhill by the same amount.

$$\Delta H_{backward} = -20 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

**Find the forward activation energy**

Activation energy is from the reactant level to the top of the curve. That is the 20 gap plus the 50 gap.

$$E_{a(forward)} = 20 + 50 = +70 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

**Check statements 1, 2 and 3**

Statement 1 matches our backward ΔH, statement 2 matches endothermic forward, statement 3 matches our Ea. All three are correct.

options.A: Correct, because all three statements are true. Forward ΔH is +20 kJ mol-1 (endothermic), so backward ΔH is -20 kJ mol-1, and forward Ea is 20 + 50 = +70 kJ mol-1.
options.B: Incorrect. This option leaves out one of the true statements. Many students doubt statement 3 because they think Ea is only 50, forgetting to measure from the reactant baseline to the peak.
options.C: Incorrect. This option leaves out one of the true statements. Many students doubt statement 1 because they confuse the sign for the reverse reaction, but reversing direction reverses the sign of ΔH.
options.D: Incorrect. This option suggests only one statement is correct. The trap is misreading the diagram levels, for example thinking the reaction is exothermic because the right side drops from the peak.
